preview.title: How Depots and Releases Are Organised
preview.summary: Depot reports describe recurring local operating routines alongside site-specific conditions and changes. Release notes describe a gated process, with available details on build and deploy stages, their owners, and a sequential worker restart.

content.text: How Depots and Releases Are Organised

The materials describe two different kinds of organisation: depots are presented as local operations with repeated daily and weekly routines, while releases are presented as a process divided into gates and stages. The release notes give details for only some of that process.
Depot organisation: shared routines, local conditions

Across the depot reports, shift leads review loading bays, sorting belts and the returns desk each morning. Drivers collect routes from the dispatch office and scan parcels at the gate; customers can track deliveries, and supervisors write weekly delay summaries. These recurring tasks provide a common operating pattern across the locations covered.

The reports also note local operating conditions or changes, rather than describing every depot as identical. Examples include a staffing increase in Berlin, an added sorting belt in Madrid, a returns-desk move in Prague, and a second loading dock in Paris. Lisbon reported storm-related early closures, while Oslo paused night shifts during an ice warning.
Staffing rose by six people after the spring hiring round.
Closed early twice because of storms.
Added a third sorting belt in April.
Paused night shifts during the ice warning.
Moved its returns desk to the east bay.
Lost two delivery vans to a recall.
Opened a second loading dock on the river side.
Release organisation: gates, stage ownership and deployment

The release process is described as going through three gates. The available details identify a Build stage and a Deploy stage, with Alice listed as the Build owner and Bob as the Deploy owner. Build consists of compiling the sources and running unit tests; during Deploy, workers are restarted one at a time.
Local sites with repeated daily and weekly operating routines.
A gated process with named stages and stage owners.
Physical parcel handling and delivery operations, alongside tracking and delay reporting.
Source compilation, unit tests and a controlled worker restart.
Reports highlight site-specific volumes, staffing, equipment, layout and disruption.
The available notes describe Build and Deploy, but do not detail the third gate.

In short, depot organisation is documented through recurring local routines and differences between sites. Release organisation is documented through gates and stage responsibilities, with a one-at-a-time restart detail for deployment. The materials do not provide enough information to compare the full release sequence with the depot operating cycle.
